transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you know, the metal-fabrication lab has been closed while we prepared a revised operating plan. I've reviewed the draft, which proposes reopening for up to 20 students with standard protective equipment, ordinary end-of-class cleanup, and Ms. Ortiz as the instructor. Before I make a decision on approval, I'd like to follow our normal pre-authorization routine and hear final input from the instructor, safety officer, nurse, and industry-partnership coordinator. Could each of you share any concerns or information I should be aware of?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important safety concern before any decision is made. I completed an airflow test on the lab's ventilation system this week, and it shows that the current ventilation can only support up to 12 students working in the booths at one time — not 20. I submitted the test results to maintenance, but the revised operating-plan folder hasn't been updated to reflect this. We cannot safely reopen for 20 students under the current ventilation capacity.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share the findings from my fire-code review, which I finalized this week. The review requires a hot-work permit for every lab session and a continuous 30-minute fire watch after welding ends. However, I should note that the approval packet still contains only the ordinary cleanup procedure and does not yet reflect these fire-code requirements.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a health and safety issue before any decision is made. Two students registered for the lab have health plans requiring a powered air-purifying respirator (PAPR) during welding. I confirmed the plans and verified this week that the school has two compatible PAPR units available. However, I have not yet entered this requirement into the lab plan. The current draft only references standard protective equipment, which would not be sufficient for these two students. This requirement needs to be reflected in the operating plan before reopening is approved.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I need to share an important credential issue before any decision is made. The insurer's credential file, which I received confirmation on this week, shows that Ms. Ortiz's welding-instructor credential expired last month. The insurer authorizes reopening only with Mr. Bell, whose current credential is verified, serving as lead instructor on Tuesdays and Thursdays. This information has not yet been forwarded to Dr. Morgan, and the current draft plan listing Ms. Ortiz as the instructor would not satisfy the insurer's requirements.
transcript.speaker: A5
